sections.html: Shawnee sits in Johnson County, part of the Kansas City metro. The 2020 count was 67,311 residents and 26,465 housing units, with 3.2% vacant. The city covers 42.86 square miles, a big footprint for a suburb, so two Shawnee houses may be miles apart with different school districts and tax levies. Pin that down first.

sections.h2: Which school district serves my Shawnee house?
sections.html:
Check the address. The city has two public districts: Shawnee Mission (USD 512) and De Soto (USD 232). A few private schools also operate inside city limits.

The district matters at sale time because it sets a large share of the tax bill. A buyer comparing two Shawnee houses will see different total levies depending on which district the parcel is in. If you know your district and can explain the bill, the buyer has fewer reasons to hesitate.

sections.h2: Property tax rates by school district
sections.html:
The combined rate is 106.066 mills in the Shawnee Mission district and 117.222 mills in the De Soto district, from the 2026 budget-year levies. The city's own levy is 23.267 mills in both areas, and the proposal for 2027 left it flat.

Residential property is assessed at 11.5% of market value. The tax is the assessed value times the mill rate, divided by 1,000.

The county appraises each parcel as of January 1, then mails Notices of Appraised Value by March 1. Tax bills follow on November 15. The appraiser's important dates page lists the whole calendar.

  • January 1: the date values are set.
  • By March 1: appraisal notices reach owners.
  • By March 31: last day to appeal, 30 days after the notice was mailed.
  • May 1: second-half bills go out.
  • May 15: informal appeals wrap up.
  • May 20: final day for appeal decisions to be mailed.
  • November 15: new tax bills go out.
  • December 20: first half, or the full amount, is due.

A spring sale often runs straight into the second-half bill. Before you fix a closing date, ask the title company how the unpaid portion will be split.

sections.h2: How to appeal your Shawnee valuation
sections.html:
The place to dispute a value is the Johnson County Appraiser, since the city has no say. When the notice arrives you may file an informal appeal, and when you pay the bill you may pay under protest instead. Only one of the two is allowed in a tax year.

File through the county's online portal or mail the Appraiser's Office in Olathe. A hearing is part of the process, and you decide whether to submit evidence only, talk by phone for 20 minutes or meet in person for 20 minutes. Protest deadlines are December 20 for owners paying their own bill, January 31 when a mortgage company pays, and May 10 for second-half or late full payments. Unhappy with the outcome? You have 30 days from the mailing date to take it to the Kansas State Board of Tax Appeals.

Appraisers must see each property at least once every six years, and a foundation crack or similar structural defect can bring a value down. Bring photos and a repair estimate.

sections.h2: Permits and yard rules before a sale
sections.html:
The city wants permits for structural jobs, electrical upgrades, demolitions, pools and hot tubs, and waives them for cosmetic interior updates. Its building permits FAQ walks through the usual cases.

  • Cabinets, doors, windows, carpet and plumbing fixtures: no permit needed.
  • Re-roofing: a permit is needed only when sheathing is added or replaced.
  • Sheds: a permit is needed over 120 square feet, with one accessory building allowed per residential lot.
  • Fences: no permit at 6 feet or less, with 6-foot fences allowed in the rear yard and 4.5-foot solid fences in the front yard.

Under the municipal code, grass on residential lots under five acres must stay below 8 inches, and on vacant lots under five acres below 10 inches. Piles of broken or worn-out items are banned on any property. Vacant and inherited houses draw most of these notices, so mow and clear the yard before showings.

sections.h2: Recording the deed in Johnson County
sections.html:
The Johnson County Register of Deeds records deeds for Shawnee property. Its fee schedule lists $21.00 for a deed or mortgage and $17.00 for each additional page. A Mortgage Registration Fee Affidavit carries no charge, and the county adds no fee for eRecording.

In a cash sale the title company or closing attorney usually handles recording, so you rarely visit the office. A deed with a missing page is the kind of problem that slows a closing, so check that every page is there before you sign.

Four situations come up again and again: inherited houses, occupied rentals, postponed repairs and deadline sales. Each is a case where a cash offer cuts out the slow steps of listing.

  • Inherited house: probate or a transfer may have to happen first, and tax bills keep coming meanwhile.
  • Tenant in place: showings are tough to arrange, which an as-is buyer sidesteps.
  • Repair backlog: failed roof sheathing, for one, can trigger a permit.
  • Tax timing: the November bill or the May second half may fall near closing.

On any route, start by collecting the newest tax statement, the notice of appraised value and any city code letter. Those three papers settle most questions from buyers and title staff.

sections.h2: Why a cash offer can fit a Shawnee house
sections.html: A buyer using a mortgage will usually ask for inspections, an appraisal and repairs, and each can slow or reshape the deal. A cash buyer looks at the house as it is and agrees on a closing date that works for you. That helps when taxes are coming due, when a tenant is in place, or when a code letter needs more work than you want to take on. If the house is in good condition and you have time, listing may reach more buyers, and we will tell you honestly which route looks better for your address.

Once an offer is accepted, the title company looks for liens and back taxes, drafts the deed and gives you a statement of what you will net. You sign the deed and seller forms at closing, then the deed goes to the county to be recorded. This year's tax bill is split with the buyer. Carry photo ID and every key, and if a mortgage is open, request the payoff figure early.

faqs.q: What is the total property tax rate in Shawnee?
faqs.a: The school district decides it. Addresses in Shawnee Mission USD 512 pay 106.066 mills combined, and those in De Soto USD 232 pay 117.222, using 2026 budget-year levies.

faqs.q: When are Shawnee property taxes due?
faqs.a: Bills are mailed November 15 and the first half or full amount is due December 20. The second-half bill goes out May 1 and is due May 10.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to replace the roof on my Shawnee house?
faqs.a: Only when sheathing is added or replaced. A plain re-roof needs none, while structural changes, electrical upgrades and demolitions do.

faqs.q: Where do I appeal my Shawnee property value?
faqs.a: With the Johnson County Appraiser's Office, using its online portal or by mail to Olathe. You have 30 days from the notice mailing, listed by the county as March 31 or earlier.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Johnson County?
faqs.a: $21.00 for a deed or mortgage, plus $17.00 for every added page. Call the Register of Deeds to confirm the current amount.
